text:
alice.m: paging in eu-west1 — increased 5xxs and higher latencies for hosted inference routes. I think it's upstream (cloud networking?) but need vendor escalation. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Pager triggered — Severity: P2. Affected service: Redwood API (generation). Avg tail latency 95th: 3.2s -> baseline 600ms. Error spike: 502/503. Links: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/123/inference /incident/1923456789
benjamin.g: on it, starting triage. @jess.sre can you grab logs + trace for recent deploys?
jess.sre: pulling traces, LB logs show connection resets to node pools in eu-west1 at 2023-06-11T14:02:xxZ. Nothing obvious in our runtime changes. Opening a cloud support case now.
marco.p: tagging partner ops (cloud provider). Drafting vendor escalation — we should include packet captures + our traceroute + exact error sample. Also need a short customer-facing status update.
alice.m: good. Benjamin, hold the canary rollout if it's still running. Add a fallback policy to route to eu-central for critical customers.
benjamin.g: canary paused. I've applied temporary routing override to steer 100% of critical-keyed traffic to eu-central. Non-critical traffic still hitting eu-west1.
incident-bot: cloud-support-bot ticket created: CS-88912, severity: urgent. Notified vendor on-call. ETA initial ack: 15m.
marco.p: draft vendor message (sending to channel so we can iterate):
```
Subject: URGENT - Networking resets impacting Redwood inference in eu-west1
Customer: Redwood Inference (prod)
Timestamp: 2023-06-11T14:02:xxZ
Description: We are observing widespread 502/503 responses and connection resets from your load balancer / transit fabric in eu-west1. Symptoms: sudden increase in TCP RSTs to our node pool, high tail latency and request failures. Impact: hosted API and dedicated customers in eu-west1.
Evidence attached: sample tcpdump + traceroute + request IDs: [rids list].
Request: Please escalate to network/backbone team and confirm whether there is a known maintenance or incident. Full packet captures available on request.
Contact: marco.p@redwood.com (ops), +1 555 0101 (pager)
```
benjamin.g: looks good. Add the manifest of affected node instance IDs and a link to our debug bundle (S3) in the evidence section. Also include the canary pause time.
marco.p: updated and sent to vendor on-call. Cloud replied: "Ack, investigating — assigned to network eng, ETA 20m for next update."
jess.sre: while we wait, drafting status page + customer email. Status page short update (copy for ops):
```
Status: Degraded performance (partial outage)
Components: Redwood API - eu-west1
Start time: 2023-06-11 14:02 UTC
Update: We are investigating increased error rates and latencies impacting the Redwood API in the eu-west1 region. Traffic is being routed to eu-central for critical customers as mitigation. We have opened a support case with our cloud provider and will provide updates every 30 minutes or when we have new information.
```
marco.p: customer notification (short):
```
Subject: Incident affecting Redwood API (eu-west1) — 14:02 UTC
Hello,
We are investigating an issue impacting API requests served from eu-west1 which may result in increased errors and latency. We’ve routed critical traffic to eu-central and opened a support case with our cloud provider. No action required from you at this time. We will follow up with updates every 30 minutes. For urgent production impact, reply to this email and we will prioritize.
```
alice.m: 👍 send the status page update and customer note now. Also prepare an internal postmortem template in the incident thread so we can capture timeline and vendor comms.
benjamin.g: status page and customer note published. Posting link: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/1923456789
incident-bot: cloud-support-bot: vendor update received — "Root cause suspected: upstream NAT gateway instability in eu-west1, mitigation: rolling NAT gateway swap underway." Next update ETA 10m.
jess.sre: good sign. Note for handoff — I'm going offline in 30m. Ben, if the vendor says NAT swap isn't enough, escalate to cloud backbone lead and request direct bridge (phone).
benjamin.g: noted. I'll keep the bridge warm. Also starting to collect affected customer list for priority outreach.
marco.p: vendor asked for logs for a specific request ID — provided r-0a1b2c3d and tcpdump link. They responded they see RSTs at the provider fabric. Asking for duration window 13:58–14:06 UTC.
alice.m: ok capture that window, attach to ticket, request a post-mortem and a timeline from them (root cause + fix timeline).
incident-bot: cloud-support-bot: vendor reports NAT gateway swap completed at 14:18 UTC. Gradual recovery observed. Monitoring for 30m.
jess.sre: I'm back — checking metrics. Error rate is falling, tail latency trending toward baseline. Re-enable partial traffic to eu-west1 for low-priority traffic in 10m.
benjamin.g: re-enabled low-priority traffic at 14:30 UTC. No regressions observed.
marco.p: sent follow-up to vendor: please include post-incident RCA and any recommended customer-facing language. Also asked them to confirm if they will notify downstream customers.
alice.m: final internal note for handoff/ops:
- Impact: partial outage / degraded performance in eu-west1, 14:02–14:30 UTC (mostly), primary cause: upstream NAT gateway instability at cloud provider.
- Mitigation: paused canary, route critical traffic to eu-central, vendor swapped NAT gateways, gradual recovery.
- Actions for PM/CS: prepare outreach for any customers with SLO breaches (list attached).
- Follow-ups: vendor RCA, attach vendor post-mortem, update postmortem timeline, add detection rule to catch sudden RST spikes.
benjamin.g: will run through handoff checklist and tag the incident in the internal tracker.
incident-bot: Incident 1923456789 status: Monitoring. Assigned: SRE oncall (benjamin.g).
alice.m: thanks everyone. Closing thread here — reopen if vendor provides new info or if errors resurge. :white_check_mark:
